grammar.title: Potential Verbs ("Can do")
grammar.explanation: Potential verbs express ability or possibility ("can do / is able to do"). All potential verbs conjugate as regular `ru`-verbs (short: `書ける / 書けない / 書けた / 書けなかった / 書けて`; long: `書けます / 書けません`).
bulletPoints: **`Ru`-verbs:** Drop final `-ru` and add `-rareru` (`見る` → `見られる`). Colloquially, shorter `ら`-less forms (`見れる`, `出れる`, `こられる` → `これる`) are common in speech, though not yet sanctioned in formal school grammar.
**`U`-verbs:** Drop final `-u` and add `-eru` (`行く` → `行ける`, `話す` → `話せる`, `待つ` → `待てる`, `死ぬ` → `死ねる`, `読む` → `読める`, `作る` → `作れる`, `泳ぐ` → `泳げる`, `遊ぶ` → `遊べる`, `買う` → `買える`).
**Irregular verbs:** `くる` → `こられる`, `する` → `できる`.
**Particles:** Verbs taking `を` can switch to `が` in potential sentences (`漢字が読める` or `漢字を読める`); `仕事をする` → `仕事ができる` (almost always `が`). Other particles (`山に登る` → `山に登れる`) remain unchanged.
**Alternative `〜ことができる`:** `Verb dictionary form + ことができる` (`ギターを弾くことができます`) keeps the original `を` particle.

grammar.title: `〜し` (Listing Multiple Reasons)
grammar.explanation: Use `[Short Form] + し` to cite two or more reasons (`(reason₁) し、(reason₂) し、(situation)`). Using a single `〜し` implies there are other unstated reasons. grammar.title: `〜そうです` ("It looks like..." — Conjecture from Appearance)
grammar.explanation: Attach `そうです` to adjective bases or verb stems to guess what something is like based on impressions when lacking conclusive evidence (so don't say `*きれいそうです` when you can already see it's pretty).
bulletPoints: **Formation:** Drop `い` from `い`-adjectives (`おいしい` → `おいしそうです`; exception `いい` → `よさそうです`); drop `な` from `な`-adjectives (`元気(な)` → `元気そうです`).
**Negative:** Replace `ない` with `なさそう` (`難しくなさそうです`, `上手じゃなさそうです`) or use `〜そうじゃないです`.
**Noun modifier & verb stems:** `そうな + Noun` (`暖かそうなセーター`); `Verb stem + そうです` for imminent events or impressions (`雨が降りそうです`, `このセーターは家で洗えそうです`).

grammar.title: `なら` (Contrast & Limitation)
grammar.explanation: `X (Noun) なら Y` means predicate `Y` applies specifically to `X` (contrasting `X` with another item, or limiting a broader category to `X`). Particles `に`, `で`, `から` can optionally appear before `なら` (`チリになら`), while `は`, `が`, `を` never appear with `なら`.

examples.en: I've been to Chile, but never to Brazil.

grammar.title: `ほしい` ("Want [something]")
grammar.explanation: `ほしい` ("want [a thing]") conjugates as an `い`-adjective (`ほしくない`, `ほしかった`), marking the desired object with `が` (or `は` in negatives). Like `たい`, `嬉しい`, `悲しい`, and `痛い`, `ほしい` is restricted to first-person descriptions (or direct questions).
bulletPoints: **Third-person desires:** Quote/guess (`ほしいと言っています`, `ほしくないでしょう`) or use the `u`-verb `ほしがる` (`ほしがっています`, which takes **`を`** instead of `が`).
**Action vs. Possession:** For wanting to *do* or *eat* something, use `Verb + たい` (`昼ご飯が食べたい`), not `ほしい`.

grammar.title: Giving & Receiving Nouns (`あげる / くれる / もらう`)
grammar.pattern: あげる / くれる / もらう
grammar.explanation: Japanese distinguishes giving/receiving verbs by direction relative to the speaker's inner circle:
bulletPoints: **`あげる` (moving away / staying away):** I give to you/others; you give to others; others give to others. `(giver) は/が (recipient) に あげる`.
**`くれる` (moving closer):** You give to me; others give to me/you (or to my close family when I identify with the benefit). `(giver) は/が (recipient) に くれる`.
**`もらう` (receiving):** `(recipient) は/が (giver) に/から もらう`. Not used when the speaker is the giver (`*(あなたは)私から手紙をもらいましたか` is wrong).

grammar.title: Volitional Form (Casual "Let's..." / "Shall I...?")
grammar.explanation: The volitional form is the casual equivalent of `〜ましょう` (used with close friends; add `か` for offers/suggestions like `手伝おうか`).
bulletPoints: **`Ru`-verbs:** Drop `-ru` and add `-yoo` (`見る` → `見よう`).
**`U`-verbs:** Drop `-u` and add `-oo` (`行く` → `行こう`, `話す` → `話そう`, `待つ` → `待とう`, `死ぬ` → `死のう`, `読む` → `読もう`, `作る` → `作ろう`, `泳ぐ` → `泳ごう`, `遊ぶ` → `遊ぼう`, `買う` → `買おう`).
**Irregular verbs:** `くる` → `こよう`, `する` → `しよう`.

grammar.pattern: Volitional Form + と思っています / と思います
bulletPoints: **`Volitional + と思っています`:** Expresses a resolution or decision already made ("I've decided to / I'm going to...").

grammar.title: Giving & Receiving Services (`〜てあげる / 〜てくれる / 〜てもらう`)
grammar.pattern: 〜てあげる / 〜てくれる / 〜てもらう
grammar.explanation: `あげる`, `くれる`, and `もらう` follow verb `て`-forms to express doing or receiving favors.
bulletPoints: **`〜てあげる`:** Doing something as a favor for someone else. Keep the main verb's particle for the beneficiary (`妹にお金を貸してあげました`), or use `〜のために` if the verb lacks a beneficiary slot (`ゆいさんのために買い物に行きました`).
**`〜てくれる`:** Someone does something for me/us (beneficiary is usually omitted; if stated, keeps the main verb's particle or `私のために`).
**`〜てもらう`:** Subject is the beneficiary who gets/persuades someone (`に`) to do something for them (or acknowledges goodwill: `知らない人に漢字を読んでもらいました`).

grammar.title: Polite & Casual Requests (`〜ていただけませんか / 〜てくれませんか / 〜てくれない？`)
grammar.pattern: 〜ていただけませんか / 〜てくれませんか / 〜てくれない？
grammar.explanation: Request favors with varying levels of politeness (descending order: `〜ていただけませんか` > `〜てくださいませんか` > `〜てもらえませんか` > `〜てくれませんか` > `〜てもらえない？` > `〜てくれない？` / bare `〜て`).
bulletPoints: **`〜ていただけませんか`:** Polite request to superiors (professors, bosses) or strangers (from `いただける`, potential of humble `いただく`).
**`〜てくれませんか`:** Polite-casual request, ideal for host families; roughly equal to `〜てください`.
**`〜てくれない？`:** Very casual request among peers.

grammar.title: Temporal Clauses (`[Clause A] 時、[Clause B]`)
grammar.explanation: `[Sentence A (short form)] 時、[Sentence B]` means "When A, B." Determine Clause A's tense by placing yourself at the time of main event B:
bulletPoints: **Present tense in A:** Event A has **not yet happened** at the time of B (`寝る時、電気を消します`; `チベットに行く時、ビザを取りました` — visa was obtained *before* going), or A is an **ongoing state/action** during B (`さびしい時`, `テレビを見ている時` — never `*行っている時`). `な`-adj take `な`, nouns take `の` before `時` (`病気の時`).
**Past tense in A:** Event A **already happened** before B (`中国に行った時、ウーロン茶を買います` — buying tea *after* arriving in China; `財布を忘れた時`).

grammar.title: Conditional `〜たら` ("If / When")
grammar.explanation: Add `ら` to any past-tense short form (`読んだら`, `読まなかったら`, `やさしかったら`, `静かだったら`, `休みだったら`) to mean "if / when A, then B."

**Constraint:** B can only happen **at or after** the time A becomes true (cannot say `*来週試験があったら、今週末勉強したほうがいい`), and `たら` requires natural dependence (not "even if").

grammar.title: Transitivity Pairs (Transitive `他動詞` vs. Intransitive `自動詞`)
grammar.explanation: Many Japanese verbs come in transitive/intransitive pairs: **transitive** verbs take an agent (`が`/`は`) and direct object (`を`), while **intransitive** verbs describe a change happening to the subject (`が`) alone.
bulletPoints: **Key pairs:** `開ける / 開く`, `閉める / 閉まる`, `入れる / 入る`, `出す / 出る`, `つける / つく`, `消す / 消える`, `壊す / 壊れる`, `汚す / 汚れる`, `落とす / 落ちる`, `沸かす / 沸く`.

grammar.title: `〜てしまう` (Completion & Regret)
grammar.explanation: `Verb て-form + しまう` has two meanings depending on context: **(1) finishing completely** ("carried out to completion") and **(2) regrettable/unintended occurrence** ("accidentally / unfortunately..."). In speech, `〜てしまう` → `〜ちゃう` and `〜でしまう` → `〜じゃう`. Because it uses the affirmative `て`-form, it is not negated to mean "regrettably didn't."

grammar.title: Honorific Verbs (`尊敬語` — Exalting the Subject)
grammar.explanation: Honorific language elevates the person performing an action (social superiors or people you don't know well—**never** use honorific verbs for your own actions!).
bulletPoints: **Special Honorific Verbs (`u`-verbs with irregular `-ます` stems ending in `-います`):**
`いる / 行く / 来る` → `いらっしゃる` (`いらっしゃいます`; also compounds like `連れていらっしゃる`)
`食べる / 飲む` → `召し上がる` (`召し上がります`)
`くれる` → `くださる` (`くださいます`)
`する` → `なさる` (`なさいます`; also compounds like `勉強なさる`)
`寝る` → `お休みになる`
`見る` → `ご覧になる`
`言う` → `おっしゃる` (`おっしゃいます`)
`〜ている` → `〜ていらっしゃる` (`〜ていらっしゃいます`)
**General Honorific Pattern:** `お + [Verb Stem] + になる` (`お帰りになりました`, `お読みになったことがありますか`). Post-predicate expressions like `〜ことがあります` and `〜ください` remain unchanged.

grammar.title: Logical Expectation (`〜はずです`)
grammar.explanation: `[Short Form] + はずです` expresses a confident expectation based on evidence, duty, or common sense ("is supposed to be / must be"). grammar.title: Extra-Modest Expressions (`丁寧語・丁重語`)
grammar.explanation: Extra-modest expressions lower your own actions (or your in-group's/company's actions) to show heightened deference to the **listener** (like adding "sir/ma'am" in formal business/interviews/announcements, often paired with `わたくし`). **Never** use them for the listener's actions!
bulletPoints: **Core vocabulary:** `いる` → `おります` (`おる`), `行く/来る` → `まいります` (`まいる`), `言う` → `申します` (`申す`), `する` → `いたします` (`いたす`), `食べる/飲む` → `いただきます` (`いただく`), `ある` → `ございます` (`ござる`), `〜ている` → `〜ております`, `〜です` → `〜でございます`.

grammar.title: Humble Expressions (`謙譲語` — Demoting the Actor to Respect the Recipient)
grammar.explanation: Humble expressions lower the actor ("I" or an in-group member) to show respect to the **person receiving or affected by the action** (contrasting with Lesson 19's `お + stem + になる` which elevates the actor).
bulletPoints: **Pattern:** `お + [Verb Stem] + する` (`お会いしました`, `お貸しする`, `お送りします`).
**`する` compound verbs:** Prefix `ご` or `お` + `する` (`ご紹介する`, `ご案内する`, `ご説明する`, `お電話する`).
**Special humble verbs:** `もらう` → `いただく`, `あげる` → `さしあげる` (note: avoid `〜てさしあげる`, prefer `お + stem + する` like `お見せしました`), `行く(visit) / 聞く(ask)` → `うかがう`.

grammar.title: Embedded Questions within Larger Sentences (`〜か / 〜かどうか`)
grammar.explanation: Embed a question inside a larger sentence using short forms:
bulletPoints: **With question words (`何`, `どこ`, `だれ`):** End with `か` (`きのう何を食べたか覚えていません`). Drop `だ` after present affirmative nouns/`な`-adjectives (`だれが一番上手か`).
**Yes/No questions:** End with `かどうか` ("whether or not"; casual speech often uses just `か`).
**Embedded `〜んです` questions:** Drop `だ` and change `ん` to `の` (`どうして来なかったのかわかりません`). Subject `は` often shifts to `が` inside embedded clauses.

grammar.title: Passive Sentences (`受身` — Suffering / Affective & Direct Passive)
grammar.explanation: In Japanese, passive sentences often express being **inconvenienced/adversely affected** ("affective passive": `(victim) は (villain) に (action) られる`), though neutral/favorable passives (`誘われました`, `尊敬されています`) and inanimate **direct passives** (agent marked with `によって` in formal writing: `この絵はピカソによって描かれました`) also exist. All passive verbs conjugate as `ru`-verbs.
bulletPoints: **Formation:** `Ru`-verbs drop `-ru` + `-rareru` (`食べる` → `食べられる`); `U`-verbs drop `-u` + `-areru` (`行く` → `行かれる`, `読む` → `読まれる`, `買う` → `買われる` with intervening `w`); Irregular `くる` → `こられる`, `する` → `される`. (Note: `u`-verb passives `読まれる` differ from potentials `読める`!)
**Constraint:** Cannot use passive for adjectives or negated verbs (`*天気に悪くされた`).

grammar.title: Intentional Resultant State (`〜が + [Transitive Verb て-form] + ある`)
grammar.explanation: `[Noun が] + [Transitive Verb て-form] + ある` describes a current state that was **intentionally arranged on purpose** by someone (often paired with prior `〜ておきました`). Contrast with intransitive `〜ている` (`窓が閉まっている`, neutral state without implying human intent) vs. `〜てある` (`窓が閉めてある`, kept closed on purpose).

grammar.title: Temporal "While / During" (`〜間に` vs. `〜間`)
bulletPoints: **`A 間に B`:** Event B (short duration) happens **at some point during** ongoing event A (`〜ている`, state verb like `いる`, or noun `留守の間`). Verb A is always in the present tense.
**`A 間 B` (without `に`):** Event B lasts **throughout the entire duration** of A.

grammar.title: Causative Sentences (`使役` — "Make / Let someone do")
grammar.explanation: Causative verbs express either **making** someone do something or **letting** someone do something (`(director) は/が (cast) に [causative verb]`). All causatives conjugate as `ru`-verbs.
bulletPoints: **Formation:** `Ru`-verbs drop `-ru` + `-saseru` (`食べる` → `食べさせる`); `U`-verbs drop `-u` + `-aseru` (`行く` → `行かせる`, `買う` → `買わせる` with `w`); Irregular `くる` → `こさせる`, `する` → `させる`.

**Particle `を` vs. `に` for the cast:** Use **`を`** for reflexive/involuntary actions (`子供を泣かせてしまいました`, `みんなを笑わせました`) or when an intransitive verb lacks a direct object `を` (`私をトイレに行かせました`, `私をそこに座らせました`). If the verb already takes `を`, use `に` (`子供に本を読ませました`).

grammar.title: Commands (`[Verb Stem] + なさい` & Imperative Form)
bulletPoints: **`[Verb Stem] + なさい`:** A firm command from a superior/parent/teacher or in exam instructions ("Do...!"). Negative instructions use `〜のをやめなさい` ("Stop doing...").

**Imperative forms (direct/aggressive, or cheering/signs like `止まれ`, `がんばれ`):** `Ru`-verbs change `-ru` to `-ro` (`やめろ`; exception `くれる` → `くれ`); `U`-verbs change `-u` to `-e` (`死ね`); Irregular `する` → `しろ`, `くる` → `こい`. Negative imperative: `[Dictionary Form] + な` (`あきらめるな`).

grammar.title: Contrast / "Despite" (`〜のに`)
grammar.explanation: `A (Short Form) のに B` connects two surprising or contradictory facts ("Even though A, B" / "Despite A, B"). Because `のに` connects two **facts**, Clause B cannot be a request, command, or suggestion (use `〜が / 〜けど` instead).

grammar.title: Causative-Passive Sentences (`使役受身` — "Be forced/made to do")
grammar.explanation: Causative-passive expresses being forced, harassed, or talked into doing something you didn't want to do (`(puppet) は (puppet master) に [causative-passive]`). All causative-passives conjugate as `ru`-verbs.
bulletPoints: **Formation:**
`Ru`-verbs: drop `-ru` + `-sase-rare-ru` (`食べる` → `食べさせられる`).
`U`-verbs ending in `す`: drop `-u` + `-ase-rare-ru` (`話す` → `話させられる`).

All other `u`-verbs (shortened `-asare-ru` form, much more common than `-aserareru`): drop `-u` + `-asare-ru` (`行く` → `行かされる`, `待つ` → `待たされる`, `読む` → `読まされる`, `取る` → `取らされる`, `泳ぐ` → `泳がされる`, `遊ぶ` → `遊ばされる`, `買う` → `買わされる` with `w`).
Irregular: `する` → `させられる`, `くる` → `こさせられる`.
